claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin Of Light', 2012, page updated 2023-05-03); https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1992ApJ...401..759M (Mitalas & Sills, ApJ 401, 759-760, both scan pages read; doi:10.1086/172103 resolves to ADS); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior', last updated 2025-01-14)
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'; 'Over tens of thousands of years, the photons travel a "drunken walk"'. MS92: 'which gives 1.7 x 10^5 yr for the diffusion time scale of the present Sun'; the common 0.5-1.0 cm step gives '3 x 10^3 to 3 x 10^4 yr, which is much too short'; the time is 'for a diffusing photon to reach the inner edge of the solar convective zone'. MSFC: 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Lowest cited figure 4e4, others 1.7e5 and ~1e6, so 'tens of thousands' is the lower bound every source supports and 'maybe far more' covers MS92/MSFC. MS92's eq. 2 (3<r^2> = N<l^2>) may overcount steps by 3 for a 3D walk (-> ~5.7e4); still tens of thousands. 'Energy' rather than 'photon' matches MSFC: 'This energy diffuses outward by radiation ... and by convective fluid flows'. Core energy is the energy that leaves: MSFC 'These reactions release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Stix 2003 not opened; nothing spoken rests on it.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html (last updated 9 May 2024); https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c (CODATA 2022); https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin Of Light', 2012, page updated 2023-05-03)
claims.note: NSSDC: radius 695,700 km; Earth distance mean 149.6, min 147.1, max 152.1 (10^6 km). NIST: c = 299 792 458 m/s exact. Photosphere to Earth = 488 s (8.14 min) to 505 s (8.42 min), mean 497 s (8.28 min). SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth.' 'Eight minutes' is the agency's own rounding.

claims.claim: 40,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale
claims.source_checked: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin Of Light', 2012, page updated 2023-05-03); https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1992ApJ...401..759M (Mitalas & Sills, ApJ 401, 759-760, both scan pages read; doi:10.1086/172103 resolves to ADS); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior', last updated 2025-01-14)
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'; 'Over tens of thousands of years, the photons travel a "drunken walk"'. (core to surface). MS92: 'which gives 1.7 x 10^5 yr for the diffusion time scale of the present Sun'; the common 0.5-1.0 cm step gives '3 x 10^3 to 3 x 10^4 yr, which is much too short'; the time is 'for a diffusing photon to reach the inner edge of the solar convective zone'. MSFC: 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. 40,000 is the lowest cited figure and the '+' is supported by MS92 and MSFC. 'Core to surface': MS92/MSFC time to the convection-zone base, after which MSFC says convection carries heat 'quite rapidly to the surface' (MS92: crossing time 'very much shorter'), so the total is still >= 4e4.
